name: Playwright
summary: Cross-browser end-to-end testing with auto-waiting and strong debugging tools.
what_it_is: A browser automation and end-to-end testing framework driving Chromium, Firefox and WebKit through one API, with automatic waiting for elements, parallel execution, and a trace viewer that records a replayable timeline of failed runs.
why_it_matters: Playwright made end-to-end tests substantially less flaky by making waiting implicit rather than something you hand-code with sleeps. The trace viewer in particular changed the economics of CI failures — you can see what happened rather than guess. It has become the default for new E2E work.
suitable_for: End-to-end testing across multiple browser engines
Teams that have abandoned E2E testing before because of flakiness
not_suitable_for: Unit testing, which it is far too heavy for
Environments that cannot run browser binaries in CI
Teams without capacity to maintain an E2E suite — the failure mode is a suite everyone ignores
verifiable_facts: Official docs describe cross-browser automation across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with auto-waiting and trace viewing.
editorial_interpretation: That it "has become the default for new E2E work".
